$comment: Lenses and methodology for each facet. Field layout and labels stay in data/elements.json (the facet registry). Adding a facet: register it in elements.json, then add it here and to at least one lens. See scripts/validate_facets.py.

lenses.label: Core Chemistry
lenses.description: Baseline context: what the element is used for.

lenses.label: Medical & Life Sciences
lenses.description: Medical and pharmaceutical uses, from cited sources.

lenses.label: Quantum & Exotic States
lenses.description: States of matter beyond the everyday: Bose-Einstein condensates of atoms, and plasma (ionised gas).

facets.label: Pharmaceutical use
facets.methodology: The record covers the element's medical and pharmaceutical use, from the cited DailyMed drug label or NIH pages, or a statement marked unaudited where no source was read. Dates are shown with each value.

facets.label: Medical imaging & implants
facets.methodology: The record covers medical imaging and implant use, from the cited USGS or peer-reviewed sources. Dates are shown with each value, and sources are listed with their retrieval date.

facets.label: States of matter
facets.methodology: Two states of matter. Bose-Einstein condensates: the condensed isotope and the year it was first realised, from the cited APS abstracts. Plasma (ionised gas): NASA Science, Sun: Facts (https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/) describes plasma as a super-hot, electrically charged gas; each element's record is from its cited NASA, NIST or NOAA page. No plasma temperatures are recorded. Elements with no cited source are not listed. Status is agent-extracted: no person has checked these values yet.
